import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Second neighborhood problem

Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture (1990) asks whether every oriented graph contains a
vertex for which there are at least as many other vertices at (directed) distance two as at
distance one.

An *oriented graph* is a finite directed graph obtained from a simple undirected graph by
assigning an orientation to each edge. Equivalently, it is a directed graph with no loops, no
parallel arcs and no two-edge cycles (digons). A Mathlib `Digraph V` is a relation on `V`, so it
has no parallel arcs by construction; we only need to require the absence of loops and digons.

The *first neighborhood* $N^+(v)$ of a vertex $v$ is the set of vertices at out-distance one
from $v$ (its out-neighbors) and the *second neighborhood* $N^{++}(v)$ is the set of vertices
at out-distance exactly two from $v$, i.e.
$N^{++}(v) = \{w \notin \{v\} \cup N^+(v) : N^-(w) \cap N^+(v) \neq \emptyset\}$.
These sets are disjoint and neither contains $v$.
A vertex $v$ with $|N^{++}(v)| \geq |N^+(v)|$ is called a *Seymour vertex*.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/second_neighborhood_problem)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [DeLa95] Dean, N. and Latka, B. J. (1995). "Squaring the tournament—an open problem."
  *Congressus Numerantium* 109, pp. 73--80.
- [arXiv:1808.02247](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02247) Dara, S., Francis, M. C., Jacob, D.,
  Narayanan, N. (2018). "Extending some results on the second neighborhood conjecture."
-/
namespace SecondNeighborhoodProblem
variable {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V)

blocks.code:
def IsOriented : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) ∧ (∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u)
blocks.docstring:
A digraph `D` is an *oriented graph* if it has no loops and no digons (two-edge cycles), i.e.
if there is an arc from `u` to `v`, then there is no arc from `v` to `u`. Since a `Digraph` is a
relation on its vertex type, it has no parallel arcs by construction.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Digraph.IsOrientation D H` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib) requires a specific simple graph H; `∃ H, D.IsOrientation H` would work but is less transparent. `Digraph.IsTournament` is too strong. Mathlib's `IsAsymm` typeclass on the relation was considered but is unidiomatic for digraphs. An API lemma proves `IsOriented D ↔ ∃ H, D.IsOrientation H`.
justification.name: SecondNeighborhoodProblem.IsOriented
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a predicate for 'oriented graph' (digraph without loops or digons) on `Digraph V`.

blocks.name: IsOriented
blocks.text:
/--
A digraph `D` is an *oriented graph* if it has no loops and no digons (two-edge cycles), i.e.
if there is an arc from `u` to `v`, then there is no arc from `v` to `u`. Since a `Digraph` is a
relation on its vertex type, it has no parallel arcs by construction.
-/
def IsOriented : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) ∧ (∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u)

blocks.code:
def outNeighborSet (v : V) : Set V :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}
blocks.docstring:
The (first) out-neighborhood $N^+(v)$ of a vertex `v` in a digraph `D`: the set of vertices at
out-distance one from `v`, i.e. the heads of the arcs leaving `v`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.neighborSet` (undirected only); Quiver-based path notions (no set of out-neighbors for `Digraph`).
justification.name: SecondNeighborhoodProblem.outNeighborSet
justification.why_needed: Mathlib's `Digraph` has no out-neighborhood / out-degree notion (only `SimpleGraph.neighborSet` exists, for undirected graphs).

blocks.name: outNeighborSet

blocks.code:
def secondOutNeighborSet (v : V) : Set V :=
  {w | w ≠ v ∧ ¬ D.Adj v w ∧ ∃ u, D.Adj v u ∧ D.Adj u w}
blocks.docstring:
The second out-neighborhood $N^{++}(v)$ of a vertex `v` in a digraph `D`: the set of vertices at
out-distance exactly two from `v`. These are the vertices `w` distinct from `v` and not in
$N^+(v)$ that are out-neighbors of some out-neighbor of `v`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.dist` (undirected, wrong notion); `Digraph.toSimpleGraphInclusive` followed by `SimpleGraph.dist` would lose orientation and misstate the problem.
justification.name: SecondNeighborhoodProblem.secondOutNeighborSet
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no directed distance for `Digraph` (`SimpleGraph.dist`/`edist` are undirected), so the set of vertices at out-distance exactly two is defined directly following the literature.

blocks.name: secondOutNeighborSet
blocks.text:
/--
The second out-neighborhood $N^{++}(v)$ of a vertex `v` in a digraph `D`: the set of vertices at
out-distance exactly two from `v`. These are the vertices `w` distinct from `v` and not in
$N^+(v)$ that are out-neighbors of some out-neighbor of `v`.
-/
def secondOutNeighborSet (v : V) : Set V :=
  {w | w ≠ v ∧ ¬ D.Adj v w ∧ ∃ u, D.Adj v u ∧ D.Adj u w}

blocks.code:
def IsSeymourVertex (v : V) : Prop :=
  (outNeighborSet D v).ncard ≤ (secondOutNeighborSet D v).ncard
blocks.docstring:
A vertex `v` of a (finite) digraph `D` is a *Seymour vertex* if its second out-neighborhood is
at least as large as its first out-neighborhood, i.e. $|N^{++}(v)| \geq |N^+(v)|$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None (could be inlined as an `ncard` inequality).
justification.name: SecondNeighborhoodProblem.IsSeymourVertex
justification.why_needed: Names the article's 'Seymour vertex' condition |N⁺⁺(v)| ≥ |N⁺(v)|, used by the main statement, the tournament variant and the tests.

blocks.name: IsSeymourVertex
blocks.text:
/--
A vertex `v` of a (finite) digraph `D` is a *Seymour vertex* if its second out-neighborhood is
at least as large as its first out-neighborhood, i.e. $|N^{++}(v)| \geq |N^+(v)|$.
-/
def IsSeymourVertex (v : V) : Prop :=
  (outNeighborSet D v).ncard ≤ (secondOutNeighborSet D v).ncard

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isOriented_iff_exists_isOrientation :
    IsOriented D ↔ ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, D.IsOrientation H := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hloop, hasymm⟩
    refine ⟨D.toSimpleGraphInclusive, fun u v huv => ⟨?_, Or.inl huv⟩,
      fun u v huv => ⟨hasymm u v, fun hvu => huv.2.resolve_right hvu⟩⟩
    rintro rfl
    exact hloop u huv
  · rintro ⟨H, hDH, hH⟩
    refine ⟨fun v hv => (hDH v v hv).ne rfl, fun u v huv => ?_⟩
    exact (hH u v (hDH u v huv)).mp huv
blocks.docstring: A digraph is an oriented graph if and only if it is an orientation of some simple graph.
blocks.name: isOriented_iff_exists_isOrientation

    rintro rfl

  · rintro ⟨H, hDH, hH⟩

theorem isOriented_directedTriangle : IsOriented directedTriangle := by
  unfold IsOriented directedTriangle

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isSeymourVertex_directedTriangle (v : ZMod 3) : IsSeymourVertex directedTriangle v := by
  have h1 : outNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 1} := by
    ext w
    simp [outNeighborSet, directedTriangle]
  have h2 : secondOutNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 2} := by
    ext w
    simp only [secondOutNeighborSet, directedTriangle, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    clear h1
    revert v w
    decide
  unfold IsSeymourVertex
  rw [h1, h2]
  simp
blocks.docstring: Every vertex of the directed triangle is a Seymour vertex.
blocks.name: isSeymourVertex_directedTriangle

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isSeymourVertex_directedTriangle (v : ZMod 3) : IsSeymourVertex directedTriangle v := by
  have h1 : outNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 1} := by
    ext w
    simp [outNeighborSet, directedTriangle]
  have h2 : secondOutNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 2} := by
    ext w
    simp only [secondOutNeighborSet, directedTriangle, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    clear h1
    revert v w
    decide
  unfold IsSeymourVertex
  rw [h1, h2]
  simp

theorem not_isSeymourVertex_digon (v : Fin 2) : ¬ IsSeymourVertex digon v := by
  have h1 : outNeighborSet digon v = {v + 1} := by
    ext w
    simp only [outNeighborSet, digon, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Seymour's conjecture, answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ oriented graph ...): 'oriented graph' means a finite digraph with no loops, no parallel arcs and no 2-cycles (digons); 'distance' is directed out-distance, so the claim is |N⁺⁺(v)| ≥ |N⁺(v)| for some v where N⁺⁺(v) is the set of vertices at out-distance exactly 2 (disjoint from N⁺(v) and excluding v); the vertex set must be assumed nonempty since the empty graph has no vertex at all.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ every finite nonempty Digraph with asymmetric adjacency (no loops, no digons; no parallel arcs by construction) has a vertex v with |N⁺(v)| ≤ |N⁺⁺(v)|, where N⁺⁺(v) = {w | w ≠ v ∧ ¬Adj v w ∧ ∃ u, Adj v u ∧ Adj u w} is exactly the set at out-distance 2 (matches arXiv:1808.02247's definition). I checked quantifier scope (all after answer(sorry)), non-strict inequality direction, Nonempty V (empty graph boundary), Set.ncard exactness under Fintype, and that answer(True)/answer(False) mean conjecture holds/fails. The final file is composed from c02 (IsOriented with explicit loop+digon clauses mirroring Digraph.IsTournament, outNeighborSet/secondOutNeighborSet, proved API lemma isOriented_iff_exists_isOrientation linking to the repo's Digraph.IsOrientation, disjointness/self-exclusion lemmas), c05/c07 (IsSeymourVertex, sink/directed-triangle/digon tests) and c07's universe-polymorphic ∀ (V : Type*) main statement. Verified in a scratch file that the composed statement body is provably equivalent to the plain inline c01/c08 formulation.

context:
In mathematics, the second neighborhood problem is an unsolved problem about oriented graphs posed by Paul Seymour. Intuitively, it suggests that in a social network described by such a graph, someone will have at least as many friends-of-friends as friends.
The problem is also known as the second neighborhood conjecture or Seymour’s distance two conjecture.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (finite, loopless, digon-free digraph; directed out-distance; N⁺⁺ disjoint from N⁺ and excluding v; nonempty vertex set) agree with the Wikipedia article and the cited papers.

namespace SecondNeighborhoodProblem

variable {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V)

/--
A digraph `D` is an *oriented graph* if it has no loops and no digons (two-edge cycles), i.e.
if there is an arc from `u` to `v`, then there is no arc from `v` to `u`. Since a `Digraph` is a
relation on its vertex type, it has no parallel arcs by construction.
-/
def IsOriented : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) ∧ (∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u)

/--
The (first) out-neighborhood $N^+(v)$ of a vertex `v` in a digraph `D`: the set of vertices at
out-distance one from `v`, i.e. the heads of the arcs leaving `v`.
-/
def outNeighborSet (v : V) : Set V :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}

/--
The second out-neighborhood $N^{++}(v)$ of a vertex `v` in a digraph `D`: the set of vertices at
out-distance exactly two from `v`. These are the vertices `w` distinct from `v` and not in
$N^+(v)$ that are out-neighbors of some out-neighbor of `v`.
-/
def secondOutNeighborSet (v : V) : Set V :=
  {w | w ≠ v ∧ ¬ D.Adj v w ∧ ∃ u, D.Adj v u ∧ D.Adj u w}

/--
A vertex `v` of a (finite) digraph `D` is a *Seymour vertex* if its second out-neighborhood is
at least as large as its first out-neighborhood, i.e. $|N^{++}(v)| \geq |N^+(v)|$.
-/
def IsSeymourVertex (v : V) : Prop :=
  (outNeighborSet D v).ncard ≤ (secondOutNeighborSet D v).ncard

/-- A digraph is an oriented graph if and only if it is an orientation of some simple graph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isOriented_iff_exists_isOrientation :
    IsOriented D ↔ ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, D.IsOrientation H := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hloop, hasymm⟩
    refine ⟨D.toSimpleGraphInclusive, fun u v huv => ⟨?_, Or.inl huv⟩,
      fun u v huv => ⟨hasymm u v, fun hvu => huv.2.resolve_right hvu⟩⟩
    rintro rfl
    exact hloop u huv
  · rintro ⟨H, hDH, hH⟩
    refine ⟨fun v hv => (hDH v v hv).ne rfl, fun u v huv => ?_⟩
    exact (hH u v (hDH u v huv)).mp huv

/-- The first and second out-neighborhoods of a vertex are disjoint. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem disjoint_outNeighborSet_secondOutNeighborSet (v : V) :
    Disjoint (outNeighborSet D v) (secondOutNeighborSet D v) :=
  Set.disjoint_left.mpr fun _ hw hw' => hw'.2.1 hw

/-- In an oriented graph, a vertex is not in its own out-neighborhood. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem notMem_outNeighborSet_self (hD : IsOriented D) (v : V) : v ∉ outNeighborSet D v :=
  hD.1 v

/-- A vertex is not in its own second out-neighborhood. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem notMem_secondOutNeighborSet_self (v : V) : v ∉ secondOutNeighborSet D v :=
  fun h => h.1 rfl

/--
**The second neighborhood problem** (Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture, 1990).

Does every oriented graph contain a vertex for which there are at least as many other vertices
at distance two as at distance one? That is, does every finite oriented graph $D$ have a vertex
$v$ with $|N^{++}(v)| \geq |N^{+}(v)|$, where $N^{+}(v)$ is the set of vertices at out-distance
one from $v$ and $N^{++}(v)$ is the set of vertices at out-distance exactly two from $v$?

The vertex set is required to be nonempty, since the empty digraph has no vertex at all.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem second_neighborhood_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] (D : Digraph V), IsOriented D →
        ∃ v, IsSeymourVertex D v := by
  sorry

/-- A sink (a vertex of out-degree zero) is a Seymour vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isSeymourVertex_of_forall_not_adj (v : V) (h : ∀ w, ¬ D.Adj v w) :
    IsSeymourVertex D v := by
  simp [IsSeymourVertex, outNeighborSet, h]

/-- The directed triangle `0 → 1 → 2 → 0` on three vertices. -/
def directedTriangle : Digraph (ZMod 3) where
  Adj u v := v = u + 1

/-- The directed triangle is an oriented graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isOriented_directedTriangle : IsOriented directedTriangle := by
  unfold IsOriented directedTriangle
  decide

/-- Every vertex of the directed triangle is a Seymour vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isSeymourVertex_directedTriangle (v : ZMod 3) : IsSeymourVertex directedTriangle v := by
  have h1 : outNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 1} := by
    ext w
    simp [outNeighborSet, directedTriangle]
  have h2 : secondOutNeighborSet directedTriangle v = {v + 2} := by
    ext w
    simp only [secondOutNeighborSet, directedTriangle, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    clear h1
    revert v w
    decide
  unfold IsSeymourVertex
  rw [h1, h2]
  simp

/--
The digon `0 → 1 → 0` on two vertices. It is not an oriented graph, and the condition excluding
digons is necessary: the digon has no Seymour vertex.
-/
def digon : Digraph (Fin 2) where
  Adj u v := u ≠ v

/-- The digon is not an oriented graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isOriented_digon : ¬ IsOriented digon :=
  fun h => h.2 0 1 (by simp [digon]) (by simp [digon])

/-- The digon has no Seymour vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isSeymourVertex_digon (v : Fin 2) : ¬ IsSeymourVertex digon v := by
  have h1 : outNeighborSet digon v = {v + 1} := by
    ext w
    simp only [outNeighborSet, digon, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    revert v w
    decide
  have h2 : secondOutNeighborSet digon v = ∅ := by
    ext w
    simp only [secondOutNeighborSet, digon, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false]
    clear h1
    revert v w
    decide
  unfold IsSeymourVertex
  rw [h1, h2]
  simp

end SecondNeighborhoodProblem

items: 'Oriented graph' is formalized as `IsOriented D := (∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) ∧ (∀ u v, D.Adj u v → ¬ D.Adj v u)` (no loops, no digons). A Mathlib `Digraph V` is a relation on `V`, so it has no parallel arcs by construction. The looplessness clause is logically redundant given asymmetry but is kept explicit for transparency (mirroring the repo's `Digraph.IsTournament`). The API lemma `isOriented_iff_exists_isOrientation` proves this agrees with the article's primary definition ('an orientation of a simple undirected graph') via the repo's existing `Digraph.IsOrientation`.

'Distance' is read as directed out-distance (as in the decomposition notes and all cited papers). N⁺(v) = {w | D.Adj v w} (out-distance one; excludes v because oriented graphs are loopless). N⁺⁺(v) = {w | w ≠ v ∧ ¬ D.Adj v w ∧ ∃ u, D.Adj v u ∧ D.Adj u w} (out-distance exactly two), which is verbatim the definition N⁺⁺(v) = {u ∈ V \ ({v} ∪ N⁺(v)) : N⁻(u) ∩ N⁺(v) ≠ ∅} from arXiv:1808.02247. The two sets are disjoint and exclude v, matching 'other vertices'.

Finiteness is imposed with `[Fintype V]` (Wikipedia: 'a finite directed graph'); cardinalities use `Set.ncard`, which is exact for subsets of a finite type. `[Nonempty V]` is required as instructed, since the empty digraph has no vertex and would otherwise trivially falsify the universal statement.

The vertex type is quantified universe-polymorphically as `∀ (V : Type*)`, following existing repo idioms (e.g. `Erdos742`). The one-vertex boundary case gives 0 ≤ 0, consistent with the conjecture (sinks are Seymour vertices; there is a test lemma for this).

'At least as many vertices at distance two as at distance one' is rendered as the non-strict inequality |N⁺(v)| ≤ |N⁺⁺(v)|; answer(True) asserts Seymour's conjecture holds, answer(False) that a counterexample exists.

Bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (namespace `SecondNeighborhoodProblem`) rather than in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`, since the task restricts output to a single file; a maintainer may prefer to move `IsOriented` / the out-neighborhood sets to `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/Digraph/` as reusable `Digraph.` definitions.
